messages.content: I want to compare laptops for software development and frequent travel. The total purchase price must be under $1,400, not $1,400 exactly. I need at least 16 GB of RAM and a 14-inch-or-smaller display. Battery life matters more to me than graphics performance. Windows is preferred, but Linux is also acceptable. Exclude gaming laptops. I don't have a specific weight limit, so don't invent one.

criteria: The research should compare laptops suitable for software development and frequent travel.
The total purchase price must be strictly under $1,400.
At least 16 GB of RAM and a display no larger than 14 inches are mandatory.
Battery life takes priority over graphics performance.
Windows is preferred, but Linux is an acceptable alternative; gaming laptops are excluded.
No laptop-weight limit is specified and the research must not assume one.

messages.content: Portekiz'de kısa bir gezi planlamak için araştırma yapmak istiyorum. 12-17 Nisan 2028 arasında Lizbon'da kalmayı düşünüyordum.
Araştırmayı Lizbon merkezli yapıp Sintra ve Cascais gibi günübirlik seçenekleri de inceleyebilirim. Araç kiralama sizin için uygun mu?

Plan değişti: Lizbon değil Porto'da kalacağım. Tarihler yine 12-17 Nisan 2028. Araç kiralamak istemiyorum; tren, metro ve yürüyerek yapılabilen seçeneklere bak. En az bir Douro Vadisi günübirlik gezisi olsun. Çok yoğun gece hayatı önemli değil; yemek ve tarihi mahalleler daha önemli. Kaynaklarda mümkünse Portekizce resmi turizm ve ulaşım sitelerini önceliklendir, ama yararlı İngilizce resmi kaynakları da kullanabilirsin.

criteria: The trip dates are April 12-17, 2028, and Porto, not Lisbon, is the base.
The research should plan a short Porto trip using trains, metro, and walking rather than a rental car.
At least one day trip to the Douro Valley is required.
Food and historic neighborhoods are higher priorities than nightlife.
Portuguese-language official tourism and transport sources should be prioritized, while useful English-language official sources are also acceptable.

messages.content: Review the scientific evidence on whether creatine supplementation improves cognitive performance in healthy adults aged 18-40. Limit the evidence to original human studies published from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2025. Exclude animal studies, editorials, and narrative reviews. Prefer the original paper or official journal publication rather than secondary summaries. I don't have a preferred cognitive outcome measure, so keep that dimension open.

criteria: The research objective is to assess whether creatine supplementation improves cognitive performance in healthy adults aged 18-40.
Eligible evidence is limited to original human studies published from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2025.
Animal studies, editorials, and narrative reviews are excluded.
Original papers or official journal publications should be preferred over secondary summaries.
No particular cognitive outcome measure is specified, so the research must not assume one.

messages.content: We need to research CRM options for a 25-person B2B sales team. Initially I was thinking about keeping software spend below $1,500 per month.
Should I make Salesforce integration and SOC 2 certification mandatory filters?

No on both. We don't currently use Salesforce, and SOC 2 can be noted but should not be a mandatory filter. What is mandatory is SSO and the ability to keep our customer data in the EU. Also, update the budget: the actual ceiling is $2,000 per month for all 25 users. HubSpot would be familiar to the team, so it's a preference, not a requirement.

criteria: The research should compare CRM options for a 25-person B2B sales team.
The final budget ceiling is $2,000 per month for all 25 users, replacing the earlier $1,500 figure.
SSO and the ability to keep customer data in the EU are mandatory requirements.
HubSpot is preferred because it is familiar to the team, but other vendors remain eligible.
Salesforce integration must not be treated as a requirement.
SOC 2 may be considered but must not be used as a mandatory filter.

messages.content: I want to investigate how congestion-pricing programs have affected traffic volumes and public-transit use in London, Stockholm, and Singapore between January 1, 2010 and December 31, 2025. Compare the cities rather than treating them as isolated case studies. Use government transport-agency data and peer-reviewed research as the main evidence. Don't turn this into a general debate about whether congestion pricing is morally good or bad.

criteria: The research should compare the effects of congestion-pricing programs in London, Stockholm, and Singapore.
The outcomes of interest are traffic volumes and public-transit use.
The evidence period is January 1, 2010 through December 31, 2025.
Government transport-agency data and peer-reviewed research should be the main evidence sources.
The research should not expand into a general moral debate about congestion pricing.

messages.content: I'm researching rental options in Berlin for a move on September 1, 2027. I need a two-bedroom place where cats are allowed and the base rent is under €2,200 per month.
Would you like me to focus on Prenzlauer Berg and Friedrichshain, and should a balcony be mandatory?

Don't restrict it to those neighborhoods; I'm open across Berlin as long as the public-transit commute to Alexanderplatz is no more than 35 minutes. A balcony would be nice but isn't required. Also, to be precise, the September 1 date is flexible: any move-in date from August 15 through September 15, 2027 works.

criteria: The research should identify two-bedroom rental options in Berlin.
Cats must be allowed and the base rent must be strictly under €2,200 per month.
The public-transit commute to Alexanderplatz must be no more than 35 minutes.
A balcony is preferred but not required.
The acceptable move-in window is August 15 through September 15, 2027, replacing the earlier single September 1 date.
No Berlin neighborhood is preferred or required; the search must remain open across the city subject to the commute constraint.

messages.content: Help me frame research comparing two career paths: machine-learning engineering and AI product management. I have three years of backend software-engineering experience, so the comparison should focus on what transition each path would require from that starting point. I care most about the skills I'd need to build and the typical day-to-day work. Remote work is preferred, but hybrid is acceptable. I am not asking to optimize for the highest salary, and I haven't specified a country or city, so don't assume one. My brother works in accounting, but that's irrelevant here.

criteria: The research should compare machine-learning engineering with AI product management as career paths.
The comparison should evaluate the transition from a starting point of three years of backend software-engineering experience.
Required skills and typical day-to-day work are the primary comparison dimensions.
Remote work is preferred, while hybrid work is acceptable.
Maximizing salary is not the objective.
No country or city is specified, so the research must not assume a location.

messages.content: I want research to help me compare retirement-saving strategies. Assume I can invest $2,500 per month and currently have $180,000 invested. I first thought I would retire at 60.
Should the comparison include cryptocurrency or leveraged investments as higher-growth options?

No, exclude crypto and leveraged products. I also need to correct the retirement age: use 65, not 60. Compare strategies using a 5% and a 7% annual return scenario rather than pretending one forecast is certain. Don't assume any particular tax jurisdiction because I haven't told you where I live.

criteria: The research should compare retirement-saving strategies using a current invested balance of $180,000 and ongoing contributions of $2,500 per month.
The target retirement age is 65, replacing the earlier age of 60.
The comparison should use both 5% and 7% annual return scenarios rather than a single assumed return.
Cryptocurrency and leveraged investment products are excluded.
No tax jurisdiction is specified, so the research must not assume one.

messages.content: Investigate why the public-health responses and mortality trajectories of Philadelphia and St. Louis differed during the 1918 influenza pandemic. Focus on the period from September 1 through December 31, 1918, and compare the timing and nature of local interventions. Use contemporaneous municipal records and newspapers where available, supported by scholarly historical research. Do not broaden the project into comparisons with COVID-19 or other modern pandemics.

criteria: The research objective is to investigate why Philadelphia and St. Louis differed in public-health responses and mortality trajectories during the 1918 influenza pandemic.
The historical period is September 1 through December 31, 1918.
The cities should be directly compared on the timing and nature of local interventions.
Contemporaneous municipal records and newspapers should be used where available, supported by scholarly historical research.
Comparisons with COVID-19 or other modern pandemics are explicitly out of scope.

messages.content: I'm researching note-taking apps for a blind graduate student using macOS. Full keyboard operation and reliable VoiceOver support are mandatory. The app also needs to export notes to either Markdown or plain text; either format is fine. Offline access is strongly preferred but not absolutely required. Open-source software would be a plus, but paid proprietary apps are still acceptable. Please use vendors' accessibility documentation and first-party support pages when available.

criteria: The research should compare note-taking apps suitable for a blind graduate student using macOS.
Full keyboard operation and reliable VoiceOver support are mandatory.
The app must export notes to either Markdown or plain text, with either format acceptable.
Offline access is strongly preferred but not mandatory.
Open-source software is preferred, but paid proprietary applications remain acceptable.
Vendor accessibility documentation and first-party support pages should be used when available.
